channel.description: Technical notes by Jaehun Ryu, a deep learning compiler engineer, on LLM inference, KV caches, compilers, C++, AI papers, and open-source code.

item.title: Intern Lumina U2: A Multi-Codebook Diffusion Large Language Model for Omni-Visual Understanding and Image Generation
item.description:
Paper

Problem: Why It’s Hard to Unify Understanding and Generation in One Representation

There have been many attempts to merge image understanding and image generation into a single model. Most, however, optimize the two abilities separately in different representation spaces. When text is trained as a token classification problem and images are trained with a diffusion/flow objective over continuous vectors, the two objectives push against each other within one backbone, which tends to make training unstable.

item.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
item.description:
Paper

Introduction

In models that handle long contexts, the compression operation that reduces multiple tokens to a single vector becomes a performance bottleneck. This paper reframes compression not as a choice of weighted averaging, but as the problem of finding the coefficients of a regression problem defined by the tokens. TTR-Compressor constructs a label-free ridge regression problem from the input tokens and uses its closed-form solution as the compressed representation.

item.title: ActionPiece: Rethinking Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
item.description:
Paper

ActionPiece: Rethinking Action Tokenization Beyond Reconstruction Error, via Physical Ranking

TL;DR — In autoregressive VLA (vision-language-action) models, the action tokenizer is the key interface that compresses continuous robot commands into discrete tokens and then reconstructs predicted tokens back into executable commands. Existing tokenizers only reduce pointwise reconstruction error such as MSE; they do not check whether the “fine adjustments” between demonstrations survive compression. This paper newly defines PRC (Physical Rank Consistency), which measures the degree to which the ranking of physical distances is preserved in the reconstructed action space, and proposes ActionPiece, which supervises representation learning and quantization jointly to preserve that relation. Under the same Qwen3-VL-4B policy training setup, it achieves state-of-the-art results of 94.8% on LIBERO and 68.8% on unseen LIBERO-Plus (source: Abstract, Table 1).

item.title: StepAudio 3 Gen Technical Report
item.description:
Paper

StepAudio 3 Gen: Unifying Speech, Song, Music, and Sound Effects with a Single Discrete Autoregressive (RVQ) Model

TL;DR

StepAudio 3 Gen, released by StepFun, is a fully discrete autoregressive generator in which a $16 \times 2048$ residual vector quantization (RVQ) tokenizer at a 12.5 Hz frame rate compresses all audio into a single shared discrete code space, a pretrained LLM predicts the first codebook $c_0$ along the time axis, and a lightweight predictor predicts the remaining 15 codebooks $c_1,\dots,c_{15}$ along the depth axis. Despite abandoning the diffusion/flow-based continuous generation paradigm, it achieves state-of-the-art on TTS and voice design (§1, §3, §7).

item.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
item.description:
Paper

Why Are Video LLMs Still So Expensive? — A Four-Stage Guide to Inference Efficiency Mechanisms

TL;DR — This paper classifies 125 VideoLLM inference efficiency studies published between late 2022 and August 2026 into 4 stages of the encoder–connector–LLM pipeline, and performs controlled comparisons only under “the same host model · the same input protocol,” concluding that accuracy is nearly preserved even when only about 25% of visual tokens remain. (source: Abstract, §I)

item.title: Janus-Pro: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Data and Model Scaling
item.description:
Paper

Janus-Pro 7B: Dual-Encoder Multimodal LLM That Outsmarts Bigger Models

One-line summary (TL;DR)

By fully separating the SigLIP understanding encoder from the VQ generation encoder and attaching them to a 7 B-parameter LLM with a ‘Dual-Encoder + Adapter’ design, it becomes the first case to beat a 13 B unified model (TokenFlow-XL) on both understanding and generation at the same time. – MMBench 79.2 (+10.3 pt) / GenEval 0.80 (+45 %)
